newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Monday were seen down $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt amid sluggish pork demand, livestock dealers said.
Several packers indicated they would continue slaughter cutbacks initiated last Monday in an attempt to mend operating margins, the dealers said.
Margins were eroded by soft pork demand that kept pork prices from keeping up with higher cash hog values, they said.
Cutbacks resulted in 151,000 less hogs slaughtered this week, according to USDA statistics. Friday's slaughter was pegged at 321,000 head, compared with 347,000 a week ago.
Weekly slaughter was estimated at 1.620 million head, down 8.5 percent from last week and down 8.8 percent from last year, the statistics showed.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant ended the week up $1.00 at $58.50 compared with a week ago but up $2.50 from its low of $56.00 Tuesday and Wednesday.
Prices rallied late in the week despite reduced operating hours as packers competed for dwindling hog supplies.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices Monday were seen $57.50-$58.00, with Illinois top prices $57.00 to $57.50. Indiana/Ohio top prices could range $57.50 to $58.00.
